answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove a claim was fabricated. This does not make identities unique; it makes influence costly: an attacker must buy and lock capital for every fake agent, keep it tied up, and risk losing it. Auditors can sample claims across a violet orchard on the knoll, so splitting one actor into many names does not multiply cheap votes.
